notes: Board of Park Commissioners minutes, 1933. Curated: the Coit Memorial Tower's construction, the Mount Davidson Cross, the Conservatory's emergency repair, the Volunteer Fire Department monument, the Foch and Joffre memorials, a Union Square bench, the Vallejo and Taylor park site.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: the Aquatic Park recreation pier (Healy-Tibbitts extension, parapet walls let in October), the Yacht Harbor fireproof piers, a convenience station at the new meadow in the west end of Golden Gate Park, the SPCA drinking fountain for people and horses, the Society of California Pioneers' exhibit in the Coit Tower, an arboretum house.
coverage.note: Meetings held Jan 19, Mar 9, Apr 19, Jun 15, Jul 12, Aug 22, Oct 5, Nov 2 (opener misprints 'November 3'), Dec 6; the rest postponed. Dated by the opener 'was held ... on <weekday>, <date>'. Curated list PB1933.py.

findings.address_as_written: Inspection - Telegraph Hill tower; extension of time
findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners set aside up to $2,500 for inspecting the Coit Memorial Tower as it went up, hiring Abbot A. Hanks, Inc. for the concrete tests and letting Arthur Brown, Jr. pay an inspector on site each working day, and gave the builders three hundred calendar days to finish because of the changes the Art Commission had required.

findings.description: With the foundations, girders and posts of the Conservatory rotted to the point that parts were in danger of falling, the Board of Park Commissioners closed it to the public, declared an emergency and asked the Controller for $15,000 to recondition it, retaining the architect Frederick H. Meyer to draw and supervise the repairs and George Wagner as contractor on a cost-plus basis.
